items.title: Classical Language Status Conferred on 5 New Indian Languages
items.summary: The Union Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi conferred the prestigious status of 'Classical Language' on five languages: Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali, expanding the total count of Classical Languages in India from 6 to 11.
items.crux: Criteria for Classical Language status include high antiquity of early texts over 1,500–2,000 years, a body of ancient literature considered valuable heritage, and original literary tradition.
takeaways: Previously 6 Classical Languages: Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu (2008), Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), and Odia (2014).
Status enables two major annual international awards for scholars, dedicated university chairs, and Centers of Excellence for studies.
Pali and Prakrit are foundational to early Buddhist canonical texts (Tripitaka) and Jain Agamas respectively.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total Classical Languages now: 11 (Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia, Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, Bengali).

mcq.question: With the recent notification in October 2024 adding Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese, and Bengali, how many languages in India now enjoy 'Classical Language' status?
mcq.explanation: With the addition of 5 new languages to the existing 6 (Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia), the total count of Classical Languages in India reached 11.

items.title: 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad Budapest: Historic Double Gold in Open and Women's Sections
items.summary: India achieved an unprecedented double gold medal triumph at the 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Budapest, Hungary, winning both the Open section (Hamilton-Russell Cup) and the Women's section (Vera Menchik Cup).
items.crux: India became only the third country in chess history (after Soviet Union and China) to win both titles at the same Olympiad, with D Gukesh, Arjun Erigaisi, Divya Deshmukh, and Vantika Agrawal also winning individual board gold medals.
takeaways: Open Team: D Gukesh, Praggnanandhaa R, Arjun Erigaisi, Vidit Gujrathi, and Pentala Harikrishna.
Women's Team: Harika Dronavalli, Vaishali Rameshbabu, Divya Deshmukh, Vantika Agrawal, and Tania Sachdev.
Gukesh posted a staggering 27-point tournament performance rating above 3050, winning 9 out of 10 games.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 45th edition; Double Gold; Open trophy: Hamilton-Russell Cup; Women's trophy: Vera Menchik Cup.

mcq.question: At the 45th FIDE Chess Olympiad in Budapest 2024, the Indian Men's team lifted which historic championship trophy?
mcq.explanation: The Hamilton-Russell Cup is awarded to the winners of the Open section, while the Vera Menchik Cup is awarded to the Women's section.

items.title: Quad Leaders' Summit in Wilmington: Quad Cancer Moonshot & MAITRI Initiative Launched
items.summary: The fourth in-person Quad Leaders' Summit convened in Wilmington, Delaware (USA), attended by leaders of India, the United States, Japan, and Australia, announcing flagship health, maritime, and semiconductor security initiatives.
items.crux: Leaders unveiled the 'Quad Cancer Moonshot' to combat cervical cancer across the Indo-Pacific and the Maritime Initiative for Training in the Indo-Pacific (MAITRI) to empower regional coast guards.
takeaways: India committed $7.5 million worth of HPV sampling kits, detection tools, and cervical cancer vaccines to the Indo-Pacific region.
Announced the first-ever 'Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission' scheduled for 2025 between the four Coast Guards.
Reaffirmed commitment to a free, open, and inclusive Indo-Pacific respecting UNCLOS maritime law.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Quad 4 nations; Flagship initiatives: Quad Cancer Moonshot, MAITRI, Semiconductor Supply Chain Contingency Network.

mcq.question: What is the primary objective of the 'Quad Cancer Moonshot' partnership unveiled at the Wilmington Quad Summit 2024?
options: Eliminating radiation exposure from nuclear submarines
Preventing and combating cervical cancer across the Indo-Pacific region
Funding lunar medical radiation testing facilities
Subsidizing chemotherapy drugs for G7 economies
mcq.explanation: The Quad Cancer Moonshot is a groundbreaking health initiative focused on expanding HPV vaccination, screening, and treatment for cervical cancer in the Indo-Pacific.

items.title: Paris 2024 Paralympics: India's Record 29 Medals & Sumit Antil Back-to-Back Gold
items.summary: India delivered its best-ever performance in Paralympic history at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, winning 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze) and finishing 18th in the overall medal table.
items.crux: Sumit Antil became the first Indian man to defend a Paralympic title with Gold in Javelin (F64, 70.59m Games Record), while Navdeep Singh secured Gold in Javelin (F41), and Avani Lekhara defended her 10m Air Rifle Gold.
takeaways: Surpassed previous best of 19 medals at Tokyo 2020 Paralympics.
Sheetal Devi (armless archer using legs) won Bronze in Mixed Team Compound Archery alongside Rakesh Kumar.
Harvinder Singh won India's first-ever Paralympic Gold medal in Archery (Men's Individual Recurve).

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) & Sports Ministry
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total: 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze); Rank: 18th; Sumit Antil: 70.59m F64 record.

mcq.question: How many total medals did India win at the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games, achieving its highest-ever tally in Paralympic history?
mcq.explanation: India won 29 medals (7 Gold, 9 Silver, 13 Bronze) at Paris 2024, placing 18th overall.

items.title: Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024: India's Largest-Ever Multilateral Air Force Combat Drill
items.summary: The Indian Air Force (IAF) conducted 'Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024', the largest multilateral air combat exercise ever hosted on Indian soil, involving air forces from over 30 countries in two phases across Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan.
items.crux: Phase 1 was conducted at Sulur Air Force Station (Tamil Nadu) featuring Germany, France, Spain, and the UK, while Phase 2 took place at Jodhpur (Rajasthan) with participation from the US, Australia, Greece, UAE, and Singapore.
takeaways: Showcased indigenous aviation platforms including LCA Tejas Mk1, Light Combat Helicopter (Prachand), and ALH Dhruv.
Marked the first deployment of the German Eurofighter Typhoon and Spanish Eurofighter fighters on Indian soil.
Strengthens interoperability, combat tactics, and strategic defence partnerships with Quad, European, and Middle Eastern allies.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Name: Tarang Shakti 2024; Participating nations: 30+; Host: Indian Air Force; First-of-its-kind multilateral air drill in India.

mcq.question: Which air base hosted Phase 1 of 'Exercise Tarang Shakti 2024', India's largest-ever multilateral air exercise?
options: Sulur Air Force Station, Tamil Nadu
Gwalior Air Force Station, Madhya Pradesh
Hindon Air Force Station, Uttar Pradesh
mcq.explanation: Phase 1 of Tarang Shakti was held at Sulur Air Force Station in Tamil Nadu, followed by Phase 2 at Jodhpur Air Force Station in Rajasthan.

items.title: Colombo Security Conclave (CSC): Founding Charter Signed for Maritime Security
items.summary: India, Sri Lanka, the Maldives, and Mauritius formally signed the founding Charter and Memorandum of Understanding establishing the Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) as a institutionalized regional security grouping in the Indian Ocean.
items.crux: CSC focuses on five core pillars: Maritime safety and security, countering terrorism and radicalisation, combating trafficking and transnational organised crime, cyber security, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief (HADR).
takeaways: Charter signed in Colombo by National Security Advisers (NSA Ajit Doval representing India).
Permanent Secretariat established in Colombo, Sri Lanka.
Bangladesh and Seychelles participate as observer states.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Member states: India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Mauritius; Observers: Bangladesh, Seychelles; 5 Security Pillars.

mcq.question: Where is the permanent Secretariat of the institutionalized Colombo Security Conclave (CSC) established?
mcq.explanation: The permanent Secretariat of the Colombo Security Conclave is located in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

items.title: INS Arighaat Commissioned: India's Second SSBN Nuclear Ballistic Submarine
items.summary: India commissioned its second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN), INS Arighaat (S3), into the Indian Navy at Visakhapatnam, cementing India's survivable nuclear triad.
items.crux: INS Arighaat joins lead vessel INS Arihant in the Strategic Forces Command (SFC), armed with K-15 Sagarika (750 km range) and K-4 (3,500 km range) submarine-launched ballistic missiles (SLBMs).
takeaways: Constructed under the Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project at Ship Building Centre (SBC), Visakhapatnam.
Powered by an indigenous 83 MW pressurized light-water reactor (PWR) using enriched uranium.
Provides an assured sea-based second-strike capability in line with India's 'No First Use' (NFU) nuclear doctrine.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Nuclear Command Authority (NCA) under Cabinet Committee on Security
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Code: S3; Class: Arihant-class SSBN; Armament: K-15 Sagarika and K-4 SLBMs.

mcq.question: INS Arighaat, recently commissioned into the Indian Navy, belongs to which category of naval vessels?
mcq.explanation: INS Arighaat is India's second indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) designed for continuous at-sea nuclear deterrence.

items.title: Digital Rupee (CBDC) Expansion: Offline Capability & Programmable Targeted Use-Cases
items.summary: The RBI introduced offline functionality and programmability for the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC / e-Rupee) in both retail (CBDC-R) and wholesale (CBDC-W) segments.
items.crux: Programmability enables targeted purpose-bound disbursements such as agricultural carbon credits or school subsidies, while offline capability enables transactions in remote low-connectivity regions.
takeaways: CBDC is a sovereign legal tender issued by the central bank in digital form, appearing as a direct liability on RBI's balance sheet.
Operates via a two-tier model where RBI issues tokens and commercial banks distribute them to retail wallets.
Interoperability with UPI QR codes allows merchants to accept e-Rupee using their existing UPI scan infrastructure.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Reserve Bank of India Act 1934 (amended by Finance Act 2022, Sec 2)
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: CBDC is fungible 1:1 with fiat currency; does not earn interest; legal tender.

mcq.question: With reference to India's Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC), consider the following: 1. It is a direct liability on the commercial banks. 2. It yields interest identical to savings bank deposits. Which is correct?
mcq.explanation: CBDC is a direct sovereign liability of the RBI (not commercial banks) and is non-interest bearing to avoid disintermediation of bank deposits.

items.title: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) Completes 10 Years: 53+ Crore Accounts & ₹2.3 Lakh Crore Deposits
items.summary: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on August 28, 2014, completed a decade of operation, achieving over 53 crore bank accounts with cumulative deposits exceeding ₹2.3 lakh crore.
items.crux: Over 55% of PMJDY account holders are women and nearly 67% of accounts are in rural and semi-urban areas, serving as the foundation of the JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) Trinity.
takeaways: Zero minimum balance requirement with a free RuPay debit card carrying ₹2 lakh accidental insurance cover.
Overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000 provided to eligible account holders.
Serves as the pipeline for Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT) across PM-KISAN, PAHAL, and scholarship welfare programs.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Launched: 28 August 2014. Motto: 'Mera Khata Bhagya Vidhata'. RuPay accidental cover: ₹2 Lakh.

mcq.question: What is the maximum overdraft (OD) facility available under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) per eligible household?
mcq.explanation: The overdraft limit under PMJDY was doubled from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000, with no conditions asked for OD up to ₹2,000.

items.title: Unified Lending Interface (ULI): RBI Launches Frictionless Digital Credit Architecture
items.summary: RBI Governor Shaktikanta Das announced the nationwide rollout of the Unified Lending Interface (ULI), a technology platform designed to enable seamless, consent-based flow of digital financial and land record data to credit institutions.
items.crux: Just as UPI transformed retail payments, ULI is designed to revolutionize lending by reducing loan appraisal turnaround times from weeks to minutes, especially for small farmers and MSMEs.
takeaways: ULI integrates data silos including state land records, satellite imagery, milk pouring data from dairy cooperatives, and Aadhaar e-KYC.
Developed by the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub (RBIH), a wholly-owned subsidiary of RBI.
Employs a 'plug-and-play' open architecture with standardized APIs, reducing documentation burden for borrower.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: ULI acronym: Unified Lending Interface; focus: rural, agriculture, and MSME credit.

mcq.question: The newly launched Unified Lending Interface (ULI) by RBI is primarily aimed at:
options: Replacing the RTGS interbank transfer network.
Enabling frictionless, consent-based credit appraisal using digitized land and financial records.
Facilitating cross-border currency trading for retail investors.
Regulating non-performing assets of urban cooperative banks.
mcq.explanation: ULI enables consent-based digital data sharing (land records, satellite data, dairy pouring data) to facilitate rapid, paperless credit evaluation.

items.title: 3rd Voice of Global South Summit (VOGSS): India Champions Developing World Priorities
items.summary: India hosted the 3rd Voice of Global South Summit virtually under the theme 'An Empowered Global South for a Sustainable Future', bringing together leaders from over 120 developing nations across Asia, Africa, and Latin America.
items.crux: Prime Minister Modi proposed a comprehensive 'Global South Development Compact' focused on trade, technology sharing, concessional finance, and human resource capacity building without imposing debt burdens.
takeaways: India operationalized the DAKSHIN (Development and Knowledge Sharing Initiative) Global South Center of Excellence.
Promotes the 'Arogya Maitri' project supplying life-saving medical supplies to crisis-hit developing nations.
Reiterates demand for reform of the UN Security Council and international financial institutions (IMF/World Bank).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Theme: 'An Empowered Global South for a Sustainable Future'; Center of Excellence: DAKSHIN; Health initiative: Arogya Maitri.

mcq.question: Which Center of Excellence was established by India to coordinate knowledge-sharing and sustainable development solutions with developing countries?
mcq.explanation: DAKSHIN (Development and Knowledge Sharing Initiative) was established by India as a specialized Center of Excellence for Global South nations.

items.title: India Adds 3 New Ramsar Sites: Total Network Reaches 85 Wetlands of Global Importance
items.summary: On the eve of Independence Day, India designated three new wetlands under the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands—Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary and Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary in Tamil Nadu, and Tawa Reservoir in Madhya Pradesh—expanding India's Ramsar network to 85 sites.
items.crux: India has the second largest network of Ramsar sites in Asia after China, with Tamil Nadu hosting the highest number of Ramsar sites in India (18 sites), followed by Uttar Pradesh (10 sites).
takeaways: Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary (Tiruppur, TN): 83rd site, an ancient large irrigation tank home to migratory waterbirds on the Central Asian Flyway.
Kazhuveli Bird Sanctuary (Villupuram, TN): 84th site, second largest brackish water lake in South India after Pulicat Lake.
Tawa Reservoir (Hoshangabad, MP): 85th site, situated inside Satpura Tiger Reserve at the confluence of Tawa and Denwa rivers.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) & Ramsar Secretariat
prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ramsar Convention 1971 & Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules 2017
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Total Ramsar sites: 85; State with most sites: Tamil Nadu (18); World Wetlands Day: 2 February.

mcq.question: Which Indian State currently possesses the highest number of Ramsar Sites (18 wetlands of international importance) in India?
mcq.explanation: Tamil Nadu leads India with 18 Ramsar sites, followed by Uttar Pradesh with 10 sites.

items.title: Paris 2024 Olympics: Manu Bhaker Historic Double Bronze in Shooting
items.summary: Manu Bhaker created history at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, becoming the first athlete in independent India's history to win two Olympic medals in a single edition of the Games.
items.crux: Bhaker won Bronze in the Women's 10m Air Pistol individual event and a second Bronze in the 10m Air Pistol Mixed Team event alongside Sarabjot Singh.
takeaways: India concluded Paris 2024 with 6 medals: 1 Silver (Neeraj Chopra) and 5 Bronze (Manu Bhaker x2, Swapnil Kusale, Men's Hockey, Aman Sehrawat).
Swapnil Kusale won India's first-ever Olympic medal (Bronze) in the Men's 50m Rifle 3 Positions event.
Aman Sehrawat (57kg Freestyle wrestling) became India's youngest individual Olympic medalist at age 21.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Indian Olympic Association (IOA) & Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Manu Bhaker: 2 medals in single Olympics; Total Paris medals: 6 (1 Silver, 5 Bronze).

mcq.question: Who became the first athlete in independent India's history to win two medals in a single edition of the Olympic Games at Paris 2024?
mcq.explanation: Manu Bhaker won two bronze medals in Paris 2024 (10m Air Pistol individual and 10m Air Pistol mixed team).

items.title: Neeraj Chopra Wins Javelin Silver at Paris 2024 Olympics (89.45m Throw)
items.summary: Reigning Olympic and World Champion Neeraj Chopra won the Silver medal in the Men's Javelin Throw at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games with a season-best throw of 89.45 meters at the Stade de France.
items.crux: Chopra became the first Indian track-and-field athlete in post-independence history to win back-to-back Olympic medals (Gold at Tokyo 2020, Silver at Paris 2024).
takeaways: Gold was won by Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem with a monstrous Olympic Record throw of 92.97 meters.
Chopra became the fourth Indian athlete in post-independence history to win multiple individual Olympic medals after Norman Pritchard, Sushil Kumar, PV Sindhu, and Manu Bhaker.
Followed by his 2023 World Athletics Championship Gold in Budapest (88.17m).

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Silver medal; Throw: 89.45 meters; Gold: Arshad Nadeem (92.97m OR).

mcq.question: Neeraj Chopra secured the Silver medal in the Men's Javelin Throw final at the Paris 2024 Olympics with a throw of:
mcq.explanation: Neeraj Chopra produced a throw of 89.45 meters on his second attempt to win the Olympic Silver medal.

items.title: SC/ST Sub-Classification Allowed: 7-Judge Constitution Bench Verdict (Davinder Singh Case)
items.summary: A landmark 7-judge Constitution Bench held by a 6:1 majority that State legislatures are constitutionally empowered to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to grant preferential reservation to more backward groups.
items.crux: The judgment overruled the 2004 5-judge bench decision in E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh, holding that SCs do not form an indivisible, homogenous class.
takeaways: Sub-classification must be based on verifiable empirical data demonstrating inadequate representation, not political expediency.
States cannot reserve 100% of seats for any sub-group, nor can they exclude any caste from the Presidential list under Article 341 entirely.
Four of the six majority judges observed that the 'Creamy Layer' principle should also apply to SCs and STs.

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Articles 14, 15, 16(4), 341, and 342 of Constitution of India
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Case: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024); Majority: 6:1 (Dissent: Justice Bela M. Trivedi).

mcq.question: Which earlier landmark judgment was overruled by the 7-judge Constitution Bench regarding sub-classification of Scheduled Castes in 2024?
options: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)
E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh (2004)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006)
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018)
mcq.explanation: The 7-judge bench overruled E.V. Chinnaiah (2004), which had previously held that SCs constitute a homogenous monolith that cannot be sub-divided.

items.title: Moidams of Assam Inscribed as India's 43rd UNESCO World Heritage Site
items.summary: The 'Moidams—the Mound-Burial System of the Ahom Dynasty' in Charaideo, Assam, was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List during the 46th World Heritage Committee session in New Delhi, becoming India's 43rd World Heritage site.
items.crux: Charaideo Moidams represents the first cultural World Heritage site from Northeast India, showcasing the 600-year-old vaulted earthen burial architecture of Tai-Ahom royals compared to the Egyptian pyramids.
takeaways: Charaideo was the first capital established by Chaolung Sukaphaa, founder of the Ahom dynasty, in 1253 CE.
A Moidam consists of a domical mound housing a vaulted brick chamber (chow-chali), covered with earth and a hemispherical earthen superstructure.
India now has 43 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (35 Cultural, 7 Natural, and 1 Mixed - Khangchendzonga).

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act 1958
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 43rd site in India; 1st cultural site in NE India; Ahom dynasty (1228-1826 CE); Founder: Chaolung Sukaphaa.

mcq.question: Which royal dynasty built the pyramidal earthen burial mound system known as 'Moidams' in Charaideo, Assam?
mcq.explanation: The Moidams are the sacred vaulted mound-burial tumuli of royalty belonging to the Tai-Ahom dynasty of Assam.

items.title: Fiscal Deficit Consolidation & New Tax Regime (Sec 115BAC) Structural Reforms
items.summary: Union Budget 2024-25 targeted a fiscal deficit of 4.9% of GDP, consolidating on track to achieve below 4.5% by FY26, alongside structural tax revisions in the default New Personal Income Tax Regime.
items.crux: Standard deduction under the New Tax Regime increased to ₹75,000 for salaried employees, tax slabs revised, and Capex outlay sustained at a record ₹11.11 lakh crore (3.4% of GDP).
takeaways: Fiscal Deficit glide path anchored under Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act 2003 principles.
Over two-thirds of personal income tax filers transitioned to the simplified New Tax Regime (Section 115BAC).
Record ₹11.11 lakh crore central capital expenditure aimed at multiplier effects on roads, railways, and urban infrastructure.

prelims_pointers.key_agency: Ministry of Finance & Department of Revenue
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Fiscal Deficit FY25 target: 4.9%; FY26 target: below 4.5%; Standard Deduction: ₹75,000; Capex: ₹11.11 Lakh Cr.

mcq.question: Under the Union Budget, what is the government's target for fiscal deficit as a percentage of GDP for financial year 2024-25?
mcq.explanation: The revised Union Budget estimated the fiscal deficit for FY 2024-25 at 4.9% of GDP, continuing the fiscal consolidation glide path to reach below 4.5% by FY26.

items.title: UPI Goes Global: Cross-Border Linkages Live in UAE, France, Singapore, Mauritius & Sri Lanka
items.summary: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) expanded Unified Payments Interface (UPI) acceptance across France (Eiffel Tower merchant payments), UAE (interlinked with AANI), Singapore (PayNow-UPI link), Mauritius, and Sri Lanka.
items.crux: Cross-border linkage enables Indian travelers and the diaspora to make instant merchant payments and inward remittances directly from rupee bank accounts via QR codes.
takeaways: Operated by NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), a wholly-owned subsidiary of NPCI incorporated in 2020.
Real-time linkage with Singapore's PayNow was India's first cross-border real-time payment system linkage.
Promotes local currency settlement, reducing reliance on intermediary SWIFT correspondent banking fees.

prelims_pointers.location: France, UAE, Singapore, Mauritius, Sri Lanka, Bhutan, Nepal
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: NPCI is an initiative of RBI and IBA under PSS Act 2007; Section 8 not-for-profit company.

mcq.question: Which subsidiary of NPCI is dedicated to deploying UPI and RuPay payment architectures internationally?
mcq.explanation: NIPL was established in April 2020 as the international arm of NPCI to drive cross-border deployment of UPI and RuPay.

items.title: 24th SCO Summit in Astana: Belarus Admitted as 10th Full Member State
items.summary: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Council of Heads of State met in Astana, Kazakhstan, officially admitting the Republic of Belarus as the 10th full member state of the Eurasian security bloc.
items.crux: Leaders signed the Astana Declaration and approved the SCO Development Strategy until 2035, affirming cooperation against terrorism, separatism, and extremism ('three evils') and promoting settlement in national currencies.
takeaways: SCO now comprises 10 member states: China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India, Pakistan, Iran, and Belarus.
External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar represented India, reiterating zero tolerance against cross-border terrorism and respect for sovereignty in connectivity.
China assumed the rotating SCO presidency for 2024–2025.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: 10th member: Belarus (joined 2024); 9th member was Iran (joined 2023); RATS HQ: Tashkent, Uzbekistan; SCO Sec: Beijing.

mcq.question: Which nation was formally inducted as the 10th full member state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at the 2024 Astana Summit?
mcq.explanation: Belarus became the 10th full member of the SCO at the Astana Summit in July 2024.

items.title: New Criminal Laws Enacted: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, BNSS & BSA Come into Effect
items.summary: Three new criminal laws—Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS 2023), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS 2023), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA 2023)—formally came into force across India, replacing the Indian Penal Code 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure 1973, and Indian Evidence Act 1872.
items.crux: The laws introduce community service as a penal punishment, mandatory videography of search and seizure, electronic Zero FIR, and replace 'sedition' with acts endangering sovereignty and unity of India.
takeaways: BNS replaces Section 124A (Sedition) with Section 152 penalizing acts endangering the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
Mandates forensic investigation for offences punishable with imprisonment of 7 years or more.
Introduces timelines for judgment delivery (within 30 days of argument conclusion, extendable to 45 days).

prelims_pointers.statutory_anchor: BNS Act 2023, BNSS Act 2023, BSA Act 2023
prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: In force from: 1 July 2024. BNS has 358 sections (IPC had 511); BNSS has 531 sections; BSA has 170 sections.

mcq.question: Under the newly enforced Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which novel category of punishment was introduced into Indian criminal law?

items.title: ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024: India Crowned World Champions Defeating South Africa
items.summary: The Indian Men's Cricket Team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024, defeating South Africa by 7 runs in the final at Kensington Oval, Bridgetown, Barbados, ending an 11-year ICC trophy drought.
items.crux: India became the first team in T20 World Cup history to win the tournament undefeated, claiming their second T20 World Cup title (first won in 2007 under MS Dhoni).
takeaways: Virat Kohli named Player of the Match in the Final (76 off 59 balls).
Jasprit Bumrah named Player of the Tournament (15 wickets at an economy rate of 4.17).
Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli formally announced their retirement from T20 International cricket following the victory.

prelims_pointers.facts_to_remember: Champions: India (2nd title); Runners-up: South Africa; Player of Tournament: Jasprit Bumrah.

mcq.question: Who was awarded the 'Player of the Tournament' award at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
mcq.explanation: Jasprit Bumrah was named Player of the Tournament for taking 15 wickets with a phenomenal economy rate of 4.17.

items.title: Indian Sovereign Bonds Included in JP Morgan GBI-EM & Bloomberg Global Indices
items.summary: Indian Government Bonds (G-Secs) under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) were formally included in the flagship JP Morgan Government Bond Index-Emerging Markets (GBI-EM) Global Diversified index with a 10% maximum weight.
items.crux: Index inclusion is estimated to trigger foreign portfolio inflows of $25–30 billion, broadening the investor base for central government debt and lowering domestic borrowing yields.
takeaways: India's weight scaled up by 1% per month until reaching the maximum cap of 10% in the index.
Only eligible dated securities issued under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) with no foreign investment caps qualify.
Bloomberg Emerging Market Local Currency Government Index also announced inclusion of Indian FAR bonds.
